correctness.summary: Folding the Gaussian likelihood ratio over coordinate signs and evaluating the resulting Gaussian quadratic integrals gives the exact determinant formula. The all-positive sign term yields the necessary lambda_max(R)<2 condition, which also makes every sign term integrable. A Kibble-Slepian/Hermite Parseval expansion gives the exact chi-square square-sum and the quartic plus squared-triangle local terms. The normalized absolute-moment Hermite coefficients give the quadratic and signed-triangle GPI expansion. Independent numerical checks reproduce the determinant formula, bivariate closed form, hypergeometric moments, and Wick identities.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The strong GPI and its moment-based Rényi certificate are prior work, quantitative bivariate GPI bounds are known, and classical/Ogasawara Gaussian absolute-moment series cover the Hermite-series methodology. The claim is restricted to the exact Rényi-2 determinant formula and lambda_max finiteness threshold for Gaussian magnitudes, the bivariate value -log(1-rho^4), the quartic/squared-triangle local expansion, and its comparison with signed-triangle GPI geometry. Searches of the recent strong-GPI and folded-normal literature did not locate these statements. Kamat (1953) and the full published Ogasawara series article were not fully inspected and remain residual risks only for moment-series formulations, for which no novelty is claimed.

value.summary: The result exactly evaluates the Rényi target that the new strong-GPI paper accesses only through a product-moment certificate, identifies a sharp spectral threshold for finiteness, and reveals a clean loss-of-sign hierarchy: GPI excess is locally quadratic with signed cubic triangle geometry, whereas Rényi dependence of magnitudes begins quartically and sees squared triangles at sixth order.

limitations: The exact formula is specialized to centered Gaussian magnitudes after marginal standardization.
The local expansions are fixed-dimensional and no dimension-uniform remainder is asserted.
The local GPI lower bound is not a global quantitative strengthening of the strong GPI.
Full texts of Kamat (1953) and the published Behaviormetrika version of Ogasawara's series paper were not inspected; no novelty is claimed for general absolute-moment series.
Independent audit has not been performed.
